Turn this on to enable certain things which are useful for a speedrun race of the ROM you create.\nThe ability to save a log file will be disabled, and a check value will be generated.\nYou can send this value around with the preset file to ensure that everyone has the same ROM to race with.
Turn this on to allow yourself to limit the Pokémon used by the randomization.\nWhen this is off all Pokémon will be allowed.

Bans "irregular" alternate formes from the Pokémon pool when "Allow Alternate Formes" is chosen for Wild Pokémon, Trainer Pokémon, Evolutions, etc.
Irregular formes are those that normally cannot exist outside of battle (such as Mega Evolutions and other in-battle transformations like Darmanitan-Z, Zygarde-C, etc),
as well as the "Fusion" Pokémon (Kyurem-B/W and Necrozma-DM/DW).
These alternate formes still exist and will get randomized base stats, abilities and so on (according to your settings),
but they can only be accessed through their regular means (such as by Mega Evolving or transforming because of an Ability).

How each Pokémon's base stats change.
• Unchanged: Don't change Pokémon stats from the base at all.
• Shuffle: Shuffle each Pokémon's stats. For example, its base Attack may be swapped with its base Special Attack, etc. This does not make any Pokémon stronger or weaker.
• Random: Randomizes each Pokémon's stats, as long as they fall within the original base stat total. This could make Pokémon stronger or weaker if they get unlucky or lucky rolls on stats they need. Evolutions of a Pokémon will be treated separately from that Pokémon unless you check Follow Evolutions.

Which Pokémon keep the Slow EXP curve when EXP curves are standardized.
• Legendaries: Slow: All legendaries get the "Slow" EXP Curve.
• Strong Legendaries: Slow: Strong legendaries get the "Slow" EXP Curve. This includes all legendaries with >600 BST.
• All Pokémon: All Pokémon get the selected EXP Curve.

When this is on, every Pokémon's EXP curve will be changed to the selected EXP curve,
except for the Pokémon forced to use the "Slow" EXP curve, chosen with the setting after this one.
This will cause Pokémon to be better or worse based more on their stats/moves/type rather than the difficulty of leveling them;
it will also allow for more potential evolutions if you randomize evolutions, since a Pokémon only can evolve into a Pokémon with the same EXP curve.

If you're not sure which EXP Curve to pick, Medium Fast and Medium Slow are generally good curves (most Pokémon use these in the regular games).

When this is on and base stats are shuffled or randomized, evolutions of a Pokémon will inherit from their base form's rolls.\nShuffle: The same new ordering of stats will be used.\nRandomized: The evolution will have the same proportion of stats as the base form.

Turn this on to update the base stats of Pokémon in the loaded game to their values in the generation chosen in the next setting.
This does NOT:
• Add any new Pokémon to the game
• Split Special Attack and Special Defense in Gen 1.

When this is on and base stats are shuffled or randomized, Mega Evolutions will inherit from their base form's rolls.
Shuffle: The same new ordering of stats will be used.
Randomized: The Mega Evolution will have the same proportion of stats as the base form.
Not recommended for use in Gen 7 unless you know what you're doing; see the Important Information page on the wiki for more info.
The generation whose base stats "Update base stats" uses.

When a Pokémon evolves, the additional BST it gains will be assigned randomly on top of the pre-evo's stats
instead of the evolved Pokémon having the exact same ratio between its stats as the pre-evo.

Applies to both regular Evolutions and Mega Evolutions (only if "Follow Evolutions"/"Follow Mega Evolutions" is chosen).

How each Pokémon's types change.
• Unchanged: Don't change Pokémon types at all.
• Random (follow evolutions): Randomize the types of each Pokémon, but make most evolutions copy the base Pokémon (except perhaps adding an extra secondary type). Evolutions that don't copy types are the Eeveelutions, among others.
• Random (completely): Randomize Pokémon types completely. Evolutions of a Pokémon are completely separate from that Pokémon, so the type of a Pokémon will likely completely change every evolution.

When this is on and types are randomized, non-split Mega Evolutions of a Pokémon will inherit that Pokémon's random types (perhaps adding another type).\nNot recommended for use in Gen 7 unless you know what you're doing; see the Important Information page on the wiki for more info.

Whether each Pokémon gets new abilities.\n• Unchanged: Don't change Pokémon abilities from the base at all.\n• Random: Give each Pokémon new abilities. Each Pokémon will have a base ability, and a 50% chance of having a 2nd ability different from the first. (50% of the species will have this ability if it is made). In Generation 5 games, each Pokémon will also receive a new random "Dream World" ability. Pokémon such as Shedinja which have Wonder Guard as their ability will keep it to maintain balance.
When this is on, Wonder Guard will be able to be chosen as any Pokémon's ability.\nThis can lead to some very overpowered/broken Pokémon.\nUSE WITH CAUTION!
When this is on and abilities are randomized, non-split evolutions of a Pokémon will inherit that Pokémon's random abilities.

When abilities are randomized, ban abilities that can prevent the opponent from fleeing/switching out from being selected.

This bans Arena Trap, Magnet Pull and Shadow Tag.

Has no effect if abilities are not randomized.

Pokémon that have a trapping ability to begin with will still have their abilities randomized, unlike how Wonder Guard is treated.

When abilities are randomized, ban abilities that are purely negative in nature from being chosen.

This bans Defeatist, Slow Start, Truant, Klutz, Stall.

Has no effect if abilities are not randomized.

Pokémon that have a negative ability to begin with will still have their abilities randomized, unlike how Wonder Guard is treated.

When abilities are randomized, ban bad abilities.

This bans Minus, Plus, Anticipation, Forewarn, Frisk, Honey Gather, Aura Break, Receiver, Power of Alchemy.
If "Double Battle Mode" for Trainers is not selected, it also bans Friend Guard, Healer, Telepathy, Symbiosis, Battery.

Has no effect if abilities are not randomized.

This setting causes abilities that have the exact same effect to be considered as the same ability for randomization probability purposes. Every variation of the respective abilities can still appear.
This applies to:
Gen 3+: Insomnia/Vital Spirit, Clear Body/White Smoke, Huge Power/Pure Power, Battle Armor/Shell Armor, Cloud Nine/Air Lock
Gen 4+: Filter/Solid Rock
Gen 5+: Rough Skin/Iron Barbs, Mold Breaker/Turboblaze/Teravolt
Gen 7+: Wimp Out/Emergency Exit, Queenly Majesty/Dazzling, Gooey/Tangling Hair, Receiver/Power of Alchemy, Clear Body/White Smoke/Full Metal Body, Multiscale/Shadow Shield, Filter/Solid Rock/Prism Armor

When this is on and abilities are randomized, non-split Mega Evolutions of a Pokémon will inherit that Pokémon's random abilities.\nNot recommended for use in Gen 7 unless you know what you're doing; see the Important Information page on the wiki for more info.

What each Pokémon evolves into.
• Unchanged: Don't randomize Pokémon evolutions.
• Random: Randomize which species each Pokémon evolves into.  Evolutions will be mostly unrestricted unless you turn on some of the evolution settings, but the EXP curves of the Pokémon must match.
• Random Every Level: Randomize which species each Pokémon evolves into while forcing them to evolve every single level. All existing evolutions for a given Pokémon will be removed and replaced with a single Level 1 evolution. Evolutions will be mostly unrestricted unless you turn on some of the evolution settings, but the EXP curves of the Pokémon must match. Evolution "loops" are expected and intended with this setting.

When this is on, random evolutions will prefer Pokémon with a similar BST to the original evolution target.\nHas less precedence than all the other evolution settings, so it may not always be strictly enforced.
When on, randomized evolutions will share at least one type between the source and target if possible.
When on, there will not be any evolution chains created that are longer than three stages.
When on, every evolution of a Pokémon will be randomized to something different than what it was originally.

When this is on, every evolution that isn't possible to do without trading in the current game will be changed.
Takes effect regardless of whether evolutions are randomized or not.
Some of the types that will be changed are:

• "Normal" trade evolutions
• Trade evolutions with another condition, such as held item or Pokémon traded for
• Day/night evolutions if there isn't day/night in the game
• Contest-stat evolutions if there aren't contests in the game
• Location-based evolutions, if those locations don't exist in the game
• Move-based evolutions, only if you randomize movesets

When this is on, Pokémon that evolve at a very high level will evolve at lower levels to make them more viable for shorter playthroughs.
Specifically, every Pokémon will evolve to its final stage by level 40, and three-stage evolutions will reach their middle stage by no later than level 30.
Additionally, Pokémon that normally evolve by having another specific Pokémon in the party will instead evolve at level 35.
Lastly, Pokémon that evolve via friendship will evolve at 160 happiness (down from 220), similar to how it works in the Switch Pokémon games.
Takes effect regardless of whether evolutions are randomized or not.
Allow Pokémon to evolve into alternate formes of Pokémon, including into regional variants.

When this is on, evolutions that require a certain time of day will now be possible regardless of the in-game time.\nSplit time-based evolutions (like Eevee => Espeon/Umbreon and Rockruff => Lycanroc) will be changed to stone evolutions instead.

Which three Pokémon are offered as starters.
• Unchanged: Don't change the starter Pokémon.
• Custom: Lets you pick the 3 starter Pokémon you want to use, or "Random" at the top of the selector.
• Random (completely): Picks 3 random starter Pokémon to be used.
• Random (basic Pokémon with 2 evolutions): Picks 3 random starter Pokémon to be used. These Pokémon must have 2 evolution stages, e.g. be like the starters in the real games.

Turning this on will randomize the items held by the starters where possible.\nIn Generation 2 games, each starter will get an individual random item.\nIn Generation 3 games, all the starters will get the same random item.
Turning this on will remove "bad" items that don't do much from the set of possible random items for starter Pokémon, such as berries and mail.
Allow alternate formes of Pokémon, such as the various formes of Rotom or Deoxys, to appear as Starter Pokémon.\nNote that their traits are randomized/shuffled separately from their base formes.

What the fixed encounters, gifts and purchases become.
• Unchanged: Static Pokémon remain the same.
• Swap Legendaries & Swap Standards: Turning this on will replace every static Pokémon encounter, gift or purchase with another random one. In this particular mode, legendary Pokémon will always be swapped for other legendaries. Also, normal non-legendary Pokémon will only be swapped for other non-legendaries. In games where Ultra Beasts appear, they will be swapped out for other Ultra Beasts.
• Random (completely): Turning this on will replace every static Pokémon encounter, gift or purchase with another random one. In this particular mode, any Pokémon can replace any other Pokémon, so you could get a Mew in the Game Corner. Or fight Magikarp instead of Mewtwo...
• Random (similar strength): Turning this on will replace every static Pokémon encounter with a Pokémon of similar strength.
Swap Statics capable of Mega Evolution with another Pokémon capable of Mega Evolution.\nThis affects Lucario in X/Y and Latios/Latias in OR/AS.
Turning this on will enable a percentage-based level modifier for every Static Pokémon.
Turning this on will enforce pure random on all static Pokémon with 600+ BST.
Allow alternate formes of Pokémon, such as the various formes of Rotom or Deoxys, to appear as Static Pokémon.\nNote that their traits are randomized/shuffled separately from their base formes.

Turning this on will set an upper BST limit on what main-game Legendary Pokémon can be randomized into, and also expand the window for what counts
as "Similar Strength" for those Pokémon.

This only applies to main-game Legendary Pokémon that are catchable and that are directly in your way during the main game, so some Pokémon
like Kyurem-B/Kyurem-W in BW2 (not catchable) and Rayquaza in Emerald (have to go out of your way to catch) are not included.

Fixes the music for all Static Pokémon encounters so that even when randomized, encounters that should have special music will play the correct song.\nNote that in Gen 4/5, if special music is assigned to a Pokémon then it will always play when battling that Pokémon, even if you just find it normally in the wild.

Which Pokémon the in-game trades ask for and give.
• Unchanged: In-game trades remain the same.
• Randomize Given Pokémon Only: Turning this on will randomize the Pokémon you receive from each in-game trade, but the Pokémon requested by the NPC in exchange will remain the same.
• Randomize Both Requested & Given Pokémon: Turning this on will replace both the Pokémon you receive from an in-game trade and the Pokémon required to do the trade.

Turn this on to randomize the nicknames of the Pokémon you receive.\nThe nicknames will be chosen from a predefined list.\nIf there are no more usable nicknames the original nicknames will be kept for the rest of the trades.

Turn this on to randomize the Original Trainer (ID & name) of the Pokémon you receive from trades.\nThe names will be chosen from the same list as trainer names,\nwith names that are too long to be OT names excluded.
Turn this on to randomize the IVs of the Pokémon you receive from ingame trades.\nIn most games these Pokémon have set IVs, so clicking this randomizes those set IVs.
Turn this on to give each Pokémon you receive from an ingame trade a random held item.\nThis includes trades that do not normally have a held item on the Pokémon.

Randomize the power of normal damaging moves.
Moves will get a new random power generally between 20 and 150 inclusive, with a very small chance of higher values appearing.
Non-damaging moves and moves with variable power will be unaffected.
NOTE: There is no way to see the updated power of moves in-game in Gen 1!

Randomize the accuracy of most moves.
Some restrictions are enforced to reduce the chances of situations like 100% accurate OHKO moves happening.
Sure-hit moves are not changed.
NOTE: There is no way to see the updated accuracy of moves in-game in Gen 1!
Randomize the PP of each move.\nThe maximum PP of each move (before PP Ups) will be randomized to a multiple of 5 between 5 and 40 inclusive.

Randomize the type of most moves.\nThe type of each move other than Struggle and ???-type moves will be re-rolled randomly.\nThis has no real effect on self-status moves, and may have odd side-effects in Gen 1.

Randomize the category of damaging moves between Physical and Special.\nThis does not affect status moves.\nNOTE: This feature is not available for Gen 1-3 games. This randomizer does NOT add the Physical/Special split to games that don't have it!

When this is on, moves will be updated to their stats (power, accuracy, etc) in the generation chosen in the next setting where possible.\nThis does NOT add the Fairy type! Moves that were changed to Fairy type will keep their Gen 5 types.\nNote that this only affects move stats, not any secondary effects that may have been added.
The generation whose move stats "Update moves" uses.

Which moves each Pokémon learns by level.
• Unchanged: Don't change Pokémon movesets at all.
• Random (preferring same type): Randomize Pokémon movesets, preferring moves that are of the type (or one of the types) of the Pokémon. Each Pokémon will get at least one reasonably accurate damaging move to begin with.
• Random (completely): Randomize Pokémon movesets, completely ignoring the type of the move and the Pokémon. Each Pokémon will get at least one reasonably accurate damaging move to begin with.
• Metronome Only Mode: Where possible, every Pokémon in the entire game will have Metronome as its only move, with the PP boosted to 40 to make it possible to complete fights without always using Struggle. Does not currently apply to non-standard battles such as the Battle Tower/Frontier or the PWT.

Turn this on to make sure every Pokémon gets a guaranteed amount of moves at level 1, instead of them keeping their original move count.\nSet how many in the next setting.\nSetting this to 4 ensures that every Pokémon you catch will have a full moveset.
Reorders the randomized movesets so that less powerful damaging moves are learned before those with high power.\n\nThe positions of non-damaging moves will not change.

Turning this on will stop moves that can break early/late games being available in randomized movesets.\nIn first generation games, Dragon Rage, SonicBoom, Spore, and every OHKO move are banned.\nIn second generation onwards, only SonicBoom and Dragon Rage are banned (because OHKO moves and sleep are significantly less broken).

Turning this on will allow you to set a proportion of the randomized movesets to be forced to be good damaging moves.\nNote that other moves can still be selected as good damaging moves randomly, this is simply an additional chance.
Set amount of guaranteed moves at level 1. Applies to all Pokémon.
Sets the probability of good damaging moves for the setting before this one.\nNote that other moves can still be selected as good damaging moves randomly, this is simply an additional chance.

Turning this on will cause every Pokémon to learn a move upon evolution.

Use carefully with Sun/Moon 1.0 - due to a glitch, if a Pokémon has an evolution move and also learns a move
on the level that it evolved at, it will only learn the evolution move upon evolving.

When this is on, the rival will have their starter in every team they battle you with, evolved if it is far enough through.\nThe rest of their team will be chosen in the same way as every other trainer.

When this is on, the random Pokémon that replaces each Pokémon will be of similar power to the original.\nHowever, preserving other rules such as type theming has precedence over this, so weaker or stronger Pokémon will be chosen if there are no other Pokémon available.

Turn this on to randomize trainers' names when you fight them.\nFor RBY, this only includes the Gym Leaders and Elite 4, as no-one else has names.\nFor every other game this will replace the names of each individual trainer.
Turn this on to randomize the class names to new names (e.g. "Youngster" could become "Misfit").

Turning this on will force all trainer Pokémon at or above the level set in the next setting to be fully evolved regardless of other settings.\nPokémon below the selected level will be randomly picked like normal.
Sets the minimum level to force fully evolved Pokémon at if that setting is on.
Sets the percentage to change trainer Pokémon levels by.\nNegative percentages (-50 to 0) will decrease levels, and positive percentages will increase them.
Turning this on will enable a percentage-based level modifier for every enemy trainer Pokémon in the game.

When this is on, the number of trainers with each type will roughly match up to the number of Pokémon with that type.\nThis should reduce repetition of Pokémon, but may lead to a lot of trainers with the same type in a row.

Pokémon such as Shedinja, with the ability "Wonder Guard", are a pain to run into early on when you can't damage them.\nTurning this on will make sure that no trainers are given these Pokémon under level 20.\nBy the time you are fighting level 20 trainers you can reasonably be expected to have a counter for each type.
Allow trainers to have alternate formes of Pokémon, such as the various formes of Rotom or Deoxys.\nNote that their traits are randomized/shuffled separately from their base formes.

Swap Trainer Pokémon capable of Mega Evolution with another Pokémon capable of Mega Evolution.\nThis only affects Trainer Pokémon that actually hold a Mega Stone (so, for example, it will affect Diantha's Gardevoir but not every Gardevoir)\nIf the "Limit Pokémon" general option is used to remove all Mega Evolutions from the game, this setting will be disabled.
Gives a 1/256 chance of Trainer Pokémon being shiny.

Turning this on will ensure that Pokémon League Trainers (Elite Four, Champions and BW1 N/Ghetsis)
are given the specified number of unique Pokémon that will not appear on any other Trainer.
The Elite Four Trainers' highest level Pokémon are the ones that will be unique;
in the case of a level tie, it will be the Pokémon further back in the party.
Does not apply to postgame Pokémon League battles.

Sets all Trainer battles to be double battles instead of single battles. The first rival battle is excluded.

Be aware that there are a few issues with this mode. In particular:

• Entering a double battle with a single Pokémon causes some generation-dependent issues:

• Gen 3: The empty spot will be filled by a duplicate of the single Pokémon, and entering the "PokÃ©mon" menu will softlock the game.
• Gen 4: The empty spot will be filled by a garbled sprite that only can use Struggle.
• Gen 6/7: The empty spot will be filled by a shiny Bulbasaur that cannot act.

• In Gen 5 games, Trainer pairs that are double battles in the regular game will have one incorrect text box if you let them spot you.
• In Gen 6 games, regular Trainers will have some text issues if you talk to them directly.

Turn this on to add additional Pokémon to "Boss" Trainers (the number is the setting itself; 0 is off). Trainers will not get more than 6 total Pokémon.\nBoss Trainers include Gym Leaders, Kahunas, Team Leaders, Elite Four, and Champions.

Turn this on to add additional Pokémon to "Important" Trainers (the number is the setting itself; 0 is off). Trainers will not get more than 6 total Pokémon.\nImportant Trainers include Rivals/Friends, Team Admins, and other important story battles (such as Colress in BW2 and Sycamore in XY).

Turn this on to add additional Pokémon to regular Trainers (the number is the setting itself; 0 is off). Trainers will not get more than 6 total Pokémon.\nRegular Trainers include all trainers that don't qualify as "Boss" or "Important" Trainers.
Turn this on to add or replace held items for the Pokémon of "Boss" Trainers.\nBoss Trainers include Gym Leaders, Kahunas, Team Leaders, Elite Four, and Champions.

Turn this on to add or replace held items for the Pokémon of "Important" Trainers.\nImportant Trainers include Rivals/Friends, Team Admins, and other important story battles (such as Colress in BW2 and Sycamore in XY).
Turn this on to add or replace held items for the Pokémon of regular Trainers.\nRegular Trainers include all trainers that don't qualify as "Boss" or "Important" Trainers.
Attempts to give Trainer Pokémon better movesets by including TM moves/tutor moves/egg moves/pre-evolution moves,\nand picking moves that synergize with the Pokémon's ability/stats/other moves.

Which species the Totem Pokémon are.
• Unchanged: Don't change Totem Pokémon species.
• Random: Randomize Totem Pokémon species.
• Random (similar strength): Replace every Totem Pokémon with a Pokémon of similar strength.

Which Pokémon the Totems call as allies.
• Unchanged: Don't change Ally Pokémon.
• Random: Randomize Ally Pokémon completely.
• Random (similar strength): Replace Ally Pokémon with Pokémon of similar strength.

Which stat boosts the Totem Pokémon's auras give.
• Unchanged: Don't change auras.
• Random: Auras will be completely randomized. The possible auras are +1/+2/+3 to a single stat or to every stat.
• Random (same strength): Auras will be randomized to auras with the same net gain of stages. For example, a Totem Pokémon that previously had +2 Speed could get +2 Defense instead. Totem Pokémon with +1/+2 to every stat will not have their auras randomized, since those auras are the only ones with 5 and 10 stages respectively.
Turning this on will enable a percentage-based level modifier for every Totem/Ally Pokémon.
Replace Totem Pokémon's held items with different consumable items.
Allows alternate formes of Pokémon to appear as Totem/Ally Pokémon.

Which Pokémon appear in the wild, and how they are placed.
• Unchanged: Don't change Wild Pokémon at all.
• Random: Completely randomize Wild Pokémon in every area. This should mean that there are many different Pokémon in each area.
• Area 1-to-1 Mapping: Each Pokémon in a given encounter area will be replaced by another Pokémon in every slot it appears in. This will make each area have a handful of random Pokémon.
• Global 1-to-1 Mapping: Every place a certain Pokémon appears in, it will be replaced by another set Pokémon. This mode doesn't support any other rules except similar strength because it is too restrictive on its own.

An extra rule for the wild Pokémon chosen.
• None: Don't apply any other rules.
• Similar Strength: When this is on, the random Pokémon that replaces each Pokémon will be of similar power to the original. However, preserving other rules such as 1-1 maps has precedence over this, so weaker or stronger Pokémon will be chosen if there are no other Pokémon available. This option is not available alongside Type Themes or Catch-em-All because the Pokémon pool would be too limited in some cases.
• Catch Em All Mode: When this is on, every random Pokémon chosen to replace an encounter will be one that hasn't been chosen before. This should make sure that every Pokémon is catchable. Once every Pokémon has been chosen the Pokémon choice list will start again from full.
• Type Themed Areas: If this is chosen, every encounter area will have only Pokémon of a random type. This may lead to a more realistic experience, or an odd one (e.g. if Fire Pokémon are chosen to be in Surfing encounters).

This affects games that have either seasons or morning/day/night encounter sets.
When this is on, each of these sets will be treated as a separate "area".
So you will have to visit each place in morning/day/night, or in each season, to collect the Pokémon.
If this isn't checked, all of morning/day/night and all seasons will use the same encounter data.

When this is on, every Pokémon in the game with a catch rate below a certain level will have its catch rate increased.

The exact minimum catch rate level is the next setting.

The percentages here assume a normal Poké Ball is used while the wild Pokémon is at full health with no status condition.

Level 1: "Normal" minimum catch rate. ~10% (Gens 1-4)/~18% (Gens 5+) chance for normal Pokémon, ~5% (Gens 1-4)/~10% (Gens 5+) chance for legendary Pokémon.

Level 2: "Buffed" minimum catch rate. ~17% (Gens 1-4)/~26% (Gens 5+) chance for normal Pokémon, ~9% (Gens 1-4)/~16% (Gens 5+) chance for legendary Pokémon.

Level 3: "Super" minimum catch rate. ~27% (Gens 1-4)/~37% (Gens 5+) chance for normal Pokémon, ~14% (Gens 1-4)/~22% (Gens 5+) chance for legendary Pokémon.

Level 4: "Ultra" minimum catch rate. ~34% (Gens 1-4)/~44% (Gens 5+) chance for all Pokémon.

Level 5: Guaranteed catches (every Pokémon is guaranteed to be caught, so long as they are catchable in the first place).

Turning this on will randomize the items held by Pokémon in the wild, including whether they can have one at all or not.\nIn some cases, these item definitions will also apply to static encounters with legendaries and the like.
Turning this on will remove "bad" items that don't do much from the set of possible random items for wild Pokémon, such as berries and mail.
Turning this on will tune down shaking grass Pokémon at lower levels.
Turning this on will enable a percentage-based level modifier for every wild Pokémon in the game.
Sets the percentage to change wild Pokémon levels by.\nNegative percentages (-50 to 0) will decrease levels, and positive percentages will increase them.

If Minimum Catch Rate is chosen, allows you to set the level used. The percentages here assume a normal Poké Ball at full health.

Level 1: "Normal" minimum catch rate. ~10% (Gens 1-4)/~18% (Gens 5+) chance for normal Pokémon, ~5% (Gens 1-4)/~10% (Gens 5+) chance for legendary Pokémon.

Level 2: "Buffed" minimum catch rate. ~17% (Gens 1-4)/~26% (Gens 5+) chance for normal Pokémon, ~9% (Gens 1-4)/~16% (Gens 5+) chance for legendary Pokémon.

Level 3: "Super" minimum catch rate. ~27% (Gens 1-4)/~37% (Gens 5+) chance for normal Pokémon, ~14% (Gens 1-4)/~22% (Gens 5+) chance for legendary Pokémon.

Level 4: "Ultra" minimum catch rate. ~34% (Gens 1-4)/~44% (Gens 5+) chance for all Pokémon.

Level 5: Guaranteed catches (every Pokémon is guaranteed to be caught, so long as they are catchable in the first place).
Allow alternate formes of Pokémon, such as the various formes of Rotom or Deoxys, to appear as Wild Pokémon.\nNote that their traits are randomized/shuffled separately from their base formes.

Which move each TM teaches.\n• Unchanged: Leave the moves in TMs as they are. If Metronome Only Mode is chosen, all TMs are changed to Metronome and this setting has no effect.\n• Random: Give each TM a new move. HM moves are not affected, nor can they be selected to be put in TMs. Each TM will still be unique. If Metronome Only Mode is chosen, all TMs are changed to Metronome and this setting has no effect.

Turning this on will stop moves that can break early/late games being available in randomized TMs.\nIn first generation games, Dragon Rage, SonicBoom, Spore, and every OHKO move are banned.\nIn second generation onwards, only SonicBoom and Dragon Rage are banned (because OHKO moves and sleep are significantly less broken).
When this is on, TMs that contain field-use moves will be left alone.\nThis includes things like Dig & Teleport, but not healing moves (Softboiled).

Turning this on will allow you to set a proportion of the randomized TMs to be forced to be good damaging moves.\nNote that other TMs can still be selected as good damaging moves randomly, this is simply an additional chance.
Sets the probability of good damaging moves for the setting before this one.\nNote that other TMs can still be selected as good damaging moves randomly, this is simply an additional chance.

Which TMs and HMs each Pokémon can learn.
• Unchanged: Every Pokémon will be able to learn the same TMs that it could before. Note that this applies even if you change the TM moves, which could lead to some odd combinations.
• Random (prefer same type): Randomize the TMs and HMs that each Pokémon can learn. Each TM or HM will have: A 90% chance of being learnable if the Pokémon has it as (one of) its type(s). A 50% chance of being learnable if the move is Normal and the Pokémon isn't. A 25% chance otherwise.
• Random (completely): Randomize the TMs and HMs that each Pokémon can learn. Each TM or HM will have a 50% chance of being learnable regardless of type.
• Full Compatibility: Select this option to allow every Pokémon to learn every TM/HM. This can be fun to mess around with, but it might make the game too easy.

When this is on and TM compatibility is randomized, evolutions of a Pokémon will inherit that Pokémon's TM compatibilities.
Additionally, when a Pokémon evolves, each TM will have:
Random (prefer same type): A 90% chance of becoming learnable if the Pokémon just gained its type through evolution, a 10% chance otherwise.
Random (completely): A 25% chance of becoming learnable regardless of type.

When this is on, then Pokémon will be guaranteed to learn TMs of moves that they learn by levelup.\nOtherwise, move compatibility will be left alone or decided randomly, depending on your other choices.
When this is on, then every Pokémon will learn every HM, regardless of any other options you check.

Which move each move tutor teaches.\n• Unchanged: Leave the moves taught by tutors as they are. If Metronome Only Mode is chosen, all Move Tutors are changed to Metronome and this setting has no effect.\n• Random: Give each move tutor slot a new move. Each Move Tutor move will still be unique, and they will not overlap with TM/HM moves. If Metronome Only Mode is chosen, all Move Tutors are changed to Metronome and this setting has no effect.
Sets the probability of good damaging moves for the setting before this one.\nNote that other tutors can still be selected as good damaging moves randomly, this is simply an additional chance.

Turning this on will stop moves that can break early/late games being available in randomized move tutors.\nIn first generation games, Dragon Rage, SonicBoom, Spore, and every OHKO move are banned.\nIn second generation onwards, only SonicBoom and Dragon Rage are banned (because OHKO moves and sleep are significantly less broken).
When this is on, move tutors that contain field-use moves will be left alone.\nThis includes things like Headbutt, but not healing moves (Softboiled).

Turning this on will allow you to set a proportion of the randomized tutors to be forced to be good damaging moves.\nNote that other tutors can still be selected as good damaging moves randomly, this is simply an additional chance.

Which move tutor moves each Pokémon can learn.
• Unchanged: Every Pokémon will be able to learn the same move tutor moves that it could before. Note that this applies even if you randomize the moves, which could lead to some odd combinations.
• Random (prefer same type): Randomize the Move Tutor moves that each Pokémon can learn. Each move will have: A 90% chance of being learnable if the Pokémon has it as (one of) its type(s). A 50% chance of being learnable if the move is Normal and the Pokémon isn't. A 25% chance otherwise.
• Random (completely): Randomize the Move Tutor moves that each Pokémon can learn. Each move will have a 50% chance of being learnable regardless of type.
• Full Compatibility: Select this option to allow every Pokémon to learn every Move Tutor move. This can be fun to mess around with, but it might make the game too easy.

When this is on and move tutor compatibility is randomized, evolutions of a Pokémon will inherit that Pokémon's move tutor compatibilities.
Additionally, when a Pokémon evolves, each move will have:
Random (prefer same type): A 90% chance of becoming learnable if the Pokémon just gained its type through evolution, a 10% chance otherwise.
Random (completely): A 25% chance of becoming learnable regardless of type.

When this is on, then Pokémon will be guaranteed to learn move tutors of moves that they learn by levelup.\nOtherwise, move compatibility will be left alone or decided randomly, depending on your other choices.

The items in item balls and hidden spots.
• Unchanged: Items on the ground and hidden items remain the same.
• Shuffle: Turning this on will take the full set of items that can be picked up from item balls, as well as hidden items, and randomize their order so each item appears in a new place. Key items are left in their original location and glitch items are excluded. This stops item balls containing seriously overpowered items, but more powerful items may be available early on. TMs will remain in the same item balls, but the numbers of the TMs in them will be shuffled among the set.
• Random: Turning this on will place a new random item in each item ball & hidden item slot. Key items & glitch items are automatically excluded. This means item balls can contain seriously overpowered items such as Master Balls. TMs will remain in the same item balls, but the numbers of the TMs in them will be randomized, including TMs not usually available from item balls. All TMs will still be available at least once in the game.
• Random (even distribution): This is the same as Random, except that the randomizer will control the number of times each item is placed. This applies to the entire game, main- and post-game.
Turning this on will remove "bad" items that don't do much from the set of possible random items for field items, such as berries and mail.

The items sold in the special (non-main) shops.
• Unchanged: Items in shops remain the same.
• Shuffle: Items in non-main shops are shuffled.
• Random: Items in non-main shops are randomized.
Turning this on will remove overpowered shop items from the pool, such as the Lucky Egg and\nitems that sell for high prices to maniacs.
Turning this on will remove "bad" items that don't do much from the set of possible random items for shop items, such as berries and mail.
Turning this on will remove regular shop items from the possible random items for shop items.
Turning this on will change prices for many items in order to make them more balanced.\nBe aware: prices for some items are seriously imbalanced without this setting.
Turning this on will ensure all evolution items appear in shops.
Turning this on will ensure all X items (including Guard Spec. and Dire Hit) appear in shops.
The items found with the Pickup ability.\n• Unchanged: Items obtained via the Pickup ability remain the same.\n• Random: Items obtained via the Pickup ability are randomized.
Turning this on will remove "bad" items that don't do much from the set of possible random items for the Pickup item table, such as berries and mail.
When abilities are randomized, ensure each Pokémon has two abilities.

Uses the post-evolution typing to determine the typing of the random evolution. Otherwise use the pre-evolution typing.\nFor example, this allows a Metapod to evolve into either a Bug- or Flying-type, instead of only a Bug-type.

Which Pokémon the trainers use.
• Unchanged: Don't change trainer Pokémon at all.
• Random: Randomize Trainers' Pokémon completely.
• Random (even distribution): For all trainers in the game (main-game and post-game), attempt to distribute Pokémon evenly.
Any other modifiers like similar strength take precedence, with the goal of reducing Pokémon from appearing too often.
• Random (even distribution, main-game): For all trainers in the game (main-game trainers only), attempt to distribute Pokémon evenly.
Any other modifiers like similar strength take precedence, with the goal of reducing Pokémon from appearing too often.
Balancing among main game trainers causes evenness with a standard playthrough, and ignores post-game trainers (they are simply random).
This setting is for Gen 5 only.
• Type Themed: Pick a type for each trainer and give them random Pokémon in that type.
Certain groups of trainers, such as the trainers in each gym, will all be given the same (random) type.
• Type Themed (Elite Four/Gyms Only): Pick a type for each trainer and give them random Pokémon in that type.
Certain groups of trainers, such as the trainers in each gym, will all be given the same (random) type.
Only applies to Elite Four and Gym Trainers/Leaders.
